Scenario fixture: listitem-parent-valid (<li> must be inside a list container)

Each target <li> has a stable id of the form lpv_case_NN. Valid parents: <ul>, <ol>, or an element with role="list".

A. Valid parents

01 — PASS: li inside ul
  • Apple
02 — PASS: li inside ol
  1. Banana
03 — PASS: li inside role="list"
  • Cherry
    • 07 — PASS: li inside ul role="presentation" (list semantics deliberately suppressed for the whole subtree — matches a widely-used reference engine's own listitem check)
    • Grape
    08 — PASS: li inside ol role="none" (role="none" is a synonym for role="presentation")
    1. Honeydew

    B. Invalid parents

    04 — FAIL: li inside a plain div
  • Date
    • 05 — FAIL: li inside role="listbox" (not "list")
  • Elderberry
    • 06 — FAIL: li inside a nav
  • Fig
    • 09 — FAIL: li inside ul role="menu" — an explicit role overrides the <ul>'s native "list" role entirely, so the tag alone no longer makes it a valid list container (found on a real site — Nike's desktop nav dropdown)
    • Kiwi

    C. The <li> itself has an explicit role (overrides its own native "listitem" role)

    10 — NEUTRAL: li role="tab" inside an invalid parent — its own explicit role overrides "listitem" entirely, so there's no listitem semantics to validate a parent for (real pattern: tablist widgets built on <li>)
  • Lemon
    • 11 — NEUTRAL: li role="menuitem" inside an invalid parent (real pattern: menu widgets built on <li>)
  • Mango
    • 12 — NEUTRAL: li role="presentation" inside an invalid parent (real pattern: HubSpot-generated nav menus)
  • Nectarine
    • 13 — FAIL: li role="listitem" (a no-op restatement, not an override) inside an invalid parent — still needs a valid list-container parent
  • Orange

    • End of fixture.
